speaker: Doctor
text: Can you describe how easy it is for you to bruise, and do your gums bleed when you brush your teeth? Also, have you noticed any unusual bleeding in your joints or muscles?

speaker: Patient
text: 4-year-old male. The child's parent reports that the child has been experiencing frequent episodes of nosebleeds and has had several instances of bleeding from the gums. Additionally, there have been occurrences of unexplained bruising and petechiae, primarily on the distal extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That history is very concerning for a bleeding disorder, such as Hemophilia or von Willebrand Disease. Does the bleeding ever start spontaneously without any injury, and does it stop on its own after applying pressure?

REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count (CBC) with Platelet Count and Peripheral Smear.
REQUEST TEST: Prothrombin Time (PT) and Partial Thromboplastin Time (PTT).

speaker: Measurement
text:
RESULTS:
Complete Blood Count (CBC) with Platelet Count and Peripheral Smear: WBC 6,500 /μL; Hemoglobin 12.1 g/dL; Platelets 280,000 /μL (normal); Peripheral Smear findings show no clumping of platelets and normal morphology of other cells.
Prothrombin Time (PT): 12 seconds (normal).
Partial Thromboplastin Time (PTT): 30 seconds (normal).

**Clinical Note:** While the standard coagulation profile (PT/PTT) and platelet count are normal, the clinical presentation of petechiae, gum bleeding, and nasal bleeding combined with the specific finding of GIIb/IIIa receptor deficiency on the ELISA Binding Assay is highly suggestive of Glanzmann's Thrombasthenia, a qualitative platelet disorder, rather than Hemophilia or von Willebrand Disease

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Frequent epistaxis. I also have Mucous membrane bleeding, Diffuse petechiae on distal extremities. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Immune Thrombocytopenia (ITP). The presentation of isolated mucous membrane bleeding and petechiae without joint bleeding, combined with the history of frequent nosebleeds, strongly suggests a platelet disorder rather than a coagulation factor deficiency. Please wait for the CBC results to confirm the platelet count.
